extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Stanford Stegner Fellowship (creative writing applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation expectations for applicants to the Stanford Stegner Fellowship in fiction or poetry, including required materials, formatting, submission rules, and what the selection committee values. Also explains administrative procedures (deadlines, fees, notifications) and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadline and submission window
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will not be accepted prior to September 1 and must be submitted online by November 3 to be considered. The application will close at 11:59 pm PST on the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note time-zone conversion (11:59 pm PST = 2:59 am EST the following day).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide personal background information, contact information for two recommenders (not letters), a writing sample (not more than 9000 words for fiction, not more than 15 pages for poetry), a statement of plans (not more than 1000 words), and a 300-word description of what they hope to get from workshops/how they will contribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee uses these items to evaluate suitability as a workshop participant; letters and transcripts are not requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a nonrefundable application fee of US$55, payable by credit card when applying online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee must be paid at time of online submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee waivers are available via a section in the online application and must be requested before the Stegner application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on fee waivers will be communicated by notification email; no waivers accepted after the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting which work to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit whatever work you feel best represents you as a writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek advice of other writers; the manuscript should show your best work and give a good feel for your writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication is not required for applying; many selected writers have publication, but admission is based on merit of the writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript form is easiest for reading, but PDFs of book excerpts or magazine pieces are accepted if legible; do not send hard-copy books (they will be discarded).

rubrics_metrics.name: No specific academic prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no required academic credentials (e.g., MFA or degree) for applicants; admission is based on merit of the writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many fellows have MFAs, but writers without formal training have been admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized tests not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send GRE, TOEFL, or any other test scores; they will not be considered and will be discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes both domestic and international applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters/transcripts not required — only recommender contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not have letters of recommendation or transcripts sent; they will not be considered and will be discarded. The application requests contact information for two recommenders so the committee may contact them if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend er contact details are for potential follow-up; the committee primarily evaluates the writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting — fiction and poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction manuscripts should be double-spaced. Poetry manuscripts may be formatted however best represents the poetry. It does not matter whether or not your name appears on each page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format to represent your work clearly; there is flexibility for poetry layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommenders' identities and relationship to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders do not have to be professors or teachers who know your writing; the committee evaluates the writing and wants to know how recommenders view your potential as a workshop participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose recommenders who can speak to your suitability for a workshop, not necessarily academic referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in fiction manuscript composition
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit any combination of pieces (one short story, 15 short stories, two novel excerpts, etc.) if that best represents you as a writer, even if that exact option isn't listed on the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee's main concern is seeing your best work and getting a good feel for your writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word/page limits for manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction manuscripts should be approximately 9,000 words. Poetry manuscripts should be 10–15 pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the expected lengths; minor excesses won't automatically disqualify, but excessively overlong submissions may be stopped from being read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over-limit submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Long applications won’t be disqualified automatically. However, the selection committee reserves the right to stop reading any applications that are heinously over the word limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions are close to stated limits to avoid being cut off from full consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible genres and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only fiction and poetry are accepted. Creative nonfiction, memoir, and screenplays are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit genres outside fiction/poetry; those manuscripts will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre considerations (science fiction/mystery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction or mystery may be submitted, but the workshop is a course in literary fiction; all manuscripts are judged as literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider that workshops involve exchanging ideas with authors who likely write outside your genre; manuscripts judged on literary criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be in English. Manuscripts not in English cannot be reviewed because workshops and readings are conducted in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit work in another language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-genre submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not apply to both poetry and fiction in the same year. Submission in both genres will disqualify the applicant from consideration in either category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose one category per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: No duplicate-category submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not submit two fiction applications or two poetry applications in the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One application per category per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applicants — paying fee
rubrics_metrics.description: International applicants may pay the application fee by credit or debit card; if they do not have a card they should email stegnerfellowship[at]stanford[dot]edu for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the program for alternative arrangements before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission confirmation and missing confirmations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants receive electronic confirmation when their application is submitted. Contact the program right away if you do not receive an emailed confirmation within a day or so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam/junk folders before contacting the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: No post-submission additions (with narrow exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee cannot alter or add information to your application, manuscript, or statement of plans after submission; the only exception is changes to your or your recommender’s contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to notify the committee of subsequent publication or awards — such information will not affect decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission of previously submitted manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: You may resubmit the same manuscript in a later year; previous applicants are encouraged to apply again and the program is interested in following applicants' growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many past fellows applied more than once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process emphasis — manuscript is primary
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts are read thoroughly and are by far the most important part of the application, followed by the statement of plans; application form information is essentially biographical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts are read by a faculty committee (not current students). Committee members discuss, reread, share promising manuscripts, and reach consensus on finalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: What the committee looks for
rubrics_metrics.description: Good fiction or good poetry — that's all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best practical advice is to seek other writers' feedback when preparing your manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of plans purpose and length
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of plans helps the committee understand why you are applying; it is intentionally open-ended and may not exceed 1000 words (most applicants submit one to two pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use it to convey motivation and fit for the fellowship; it is secondary to the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification policy and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants will be notified of their status by April 1; applicants should not contact the program before then about their application status (except to update contact information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications are strictly boolean; the program will not indicate shortlist status or provide feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: No shortlist/disclosure or feedback policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will not disclose whether an applicant was shortlisted, will not tell applicants if they are out of contention, and will not provide feedback on manuscripts or reasons for non-selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy helps keep the application fee reasonable given high volume of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender contact timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee does not necessarily contact recommenders of successful applicants, and if they do they may do so at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not try to use recommenders to gauge application status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are offered for the following two academic years and may not be deferred; if selected, you cannot postpone admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan availability accordingly before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant pool size and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 1,500 applications were received for 10 fellowships in a recent year, indicating high competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of the competitive ratio and prepare submissions accordingly.
